. A técnica central é o prompting aumentado por memória (memory-augmented prompting), que recupera exemplos de programas de linguagem relevantes para a instrução de entrada e os utiliza como exemplos no prompt do LLM
. Além disso, o HELPER-X utiliza Geração Aumentada por Recuperação (RAG) para integrar fontes de conhecimento externas
. O modelo não requer treinamento específico no domínio (in-domain training) para alcançar desempenho de estado da arte
.
QP6 - Os dados utilizados para treino/teste/validação são explicados em sua completude e faz sentido para o problema alvo? Sim. O trabalho utiliza quatro benchmarks diversos e consolidados na área de agentes incorporados (embodied agents): TEACh (diálogos para tarefas domésticas), ALFRED (seguimento de instruções de linguagem natural), DialFRED (instruções com perguntas ativas) e Tidy Task (reorganização de quartos usando senso comum)
. Cada conjunto de dados é detalhado quanto ao número de demonstrações, tipos de tarefas e ambientes (baseados no simulador AI2-THOR), garantindo que as avaliações cubram as capacidades de planejamento, percepção e interação pretendidas
.
QP7 - Os critérios de avaliação da arquitetura permitem avaliar várias tarefas multimodalidade? Sim. Os critérios incluem a Taxa de Sucesso da Tarefa (SR) e a Taxa de Sucesso de Condição de Meta (GC), além de variantes ponderadas pelo comprimento do caminho
. No Tidy Task, são usadas métricas específicas como Objetos Movidos Corretamente (CM), Objetos Movidos Incorretamente (IM) e uma métrica de Energia que avalia a conformidade da organização do quarto com padrões humanos
. Essas métricas avaliam a integração entre a compreensão da linguagem (instruções/diálogos), a percepção visual (identificação de objetos) e a execução motora
.

P414.title: LLaVA-Plus: Learning to Use Tools for Creating Multimodal Agents
P414.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2
P414.notas:
QP1 - Quais métodos de aprendizado são explorados? O LLaVA-Plus utiliza uma abordagem de treinamento ponta a ponta (end-to-end) para expandir sistematicamente as capacidades de modelos multimodais de larga escala (LMMs)
. As principais técnicas e métodos computacionais incluem:
Visual Instruction Tuning (Ajuste de Instrução Visual): O modelo é treinado seguindo o paradigma de ajuste de instruções multimodais para aprender a usar ferramentas externas
.
Self-Instruct: Utiliza-se o método de "auto-instrução" para curar dados, alavancando modelos como ChatGPT e GPT-4 como rotuladores (labelers) para gerar diálogos de acompanhamento de instruções
.
Objetivo Auto-regressivo: O treinamento é realizado com um objetivo de predição auto-regressiva em uma arquitetura baseada em Transformer
.
Aprendizado de Chaining de Ferramentas (Tool Chaining): O método ensina o modelo a atuar como um planejador que seleciona, compõe e ativa ferramentas de um repositório de habilidades
.
Cadeia de Pensamento (Chain-of-Thought): O formato de dados inclui um campo de "Pensamento" (Thought) para representar o processo de raciocínio antes da ação
.
QP5 - A arquitetura consta algum módulo de visualização computacional para explicabilidade de treino ou teste? Sim, a arquitetura oferece explicabilidade através de dois componentes principais:
Módulo de Raciocínio Textual (Field "Thought"): Antes de executar uma ação, o modelo gera um texto descrevendo seu processo de raciocínio, determinando se precisa de ferramentas e quais usar
.
Visualização de Resultados de Ferramentas: O sistema utiliza modelos especialistas (como Grounding DINO para detecção e SAM para segmentação) cujos resultados (caixas delimitadoras e máscaras) são visualizados diretamente sobre a imagem original, tornando a decisão do modelo intuitiva para o usuário
.
QP6 - Os dados utilizados para treino/teste/validação são explicados em sua completude e faz sentido para o problema alvo? Sim. O pipeline de geração de dados é detalhado, abrangendo habilidades de compreensão visual, geração e recuperação de conhecimento externo
. São utilizados datasets públicos consolidados como COCO (objetos e segmentação), HierText (OCR), InfoSeek (conhecimento externo), JourneyDB e InstructPix2Pix (geração e edição de imagens)
. A combinação desses dados faz sentido direto para o objetivo de criar um agente capaz de interagir e manipular ferramentas visuais no mundo real
.
QP7 - Os critérios de avaliação da arquitetura permitem avaliar várias tarefas multimodalidade? Sim. O LLaVA-Plus é avaliado em diversos benchmarks que cobrem múltiplas facetas:
LLaVA-Bench (COCO e In-the-Wild): Avalia conversação, descrição detalhada e raciocínio visual
.
SEED-Bench: Mede percepção e raciocínio nos níveis de imagem e instância
.
MM-Vet: Avalia seis capacidades principais de visão-linguagem e suas integrações
.
VisIT-Bench: Foca no acompanhamento de instruções em cenários da vida real
.
LLaVA-Bench (Tools): Um conjunto criado especificamente para medir habilidades de grounding, tagging, legendagem e OCR
.

P415.title: Group Generalized Mean Pooling for Vision Transformer
P415.notas:
QP1 - Quais métodos de aprendizado são explorados? O trabalho explora diversos métodos de aprendizado de máquina aplicados à visão computacional, incluindo:
Aprendizado Supervisionado: Treino do zero (scratch training) e ajuste fino (fine-tuning) em tarefas de classificação de imagem
.
Aprendizado Auto-Supervisionado (Self-Supervised Learning - SSL): O documento valida a técnica GGeM em modelos pré-treinados com MAE (Masked Autoencoders), BeiT, SimMIM e Data2Vec
.
Aprendizado de Representação Multimodal: Treinamento de modelos visão-linguagem (como o CLIP) para alinhar representações de texto e imagem
.
Transfer Learning: Avaliação através de Linear Probing e Partial Fine-tuning (ajuste fino de apenas alguns blocos do Transformer)
.
Deep Metric Learning: Utilizado em tarefas de recuperação de imagem com a função de perda Norm-softmax
.
QP5 - A arquitetura consta algum módulo de visualização computacional para explicabilidade de treino ou teste? Sim. O trabalho utiliza várias técnicas de visualização e análise para explicabilidade:
Score-CAM: Uma variante do Class Activation Map utilizada para visualizar as decisões do modelo com base na importância espacial dos patches de imagem
.
Visualização de Mapas de Ativação: Utilizada para demonstrar como diferentes parâmetros de pooling afetam a concentração do gradiente e a resposta local vs. global do modelo
.
Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA): Técnica para analisar a similaridade entre as representações das diferentes cabeças de atenção, demonstrando que o GGeM reduz a redundância entre elas
.
Attention Head Mean Distance: Visualização que pondera a distância dos pixels pelos pesos de atenção para entender se as cabeças focam em informações locais ou globais
.
QP6 - Os dados utilizados para treino/teste/validação são explicados em sua completude e faz sentido para o problema alvo? Sim. O documento utiliza diversos conjuntos de dados consolidados na literatura para validar a versatilidade da técnica:
ImageNet-1K: Para classificação e pré-treinamento de modelos ViT-Small, Base e Large
.
CUB200, Cars196 e Stanford Online Products (SOP): Para tarefas de recuperação de imagem (image retrieval)
.
Conceptual Captions (CC3M), Flickr30k e MSCOCO: Para aprendizado multimodal e recuperação cruzada entre imagem e texto
.
ImageNet-9 (IN-9): Para avaliar a robustez do modelo contra variações de fundo
. O uso desses dados é adequado, pois permite avaliar se o novo método de pooling (GGeM) melhora a agregação de informações espaciais em diferentes contextos de visão e linguagem
.
QP7 - Os critérios de avaliação da arquitetura permitem avaliar várias tarefas multimodalidade? Sim. A arquitetura é avaliada em tarefas de zero-shot classification em diversos datasets (como CIFAR-10, EuroSAT e MNIST) e em zero-shot cross-modal retrieval (recuperação de imagem para texto e vice-versa) nos benchmarks Flickr30k e MSCOCO
.

P416.title: Retrieval Augmentation for Deep Neural Networks
P416.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2
P416.notas:
QP1 - Quais métodos de aprendizado são explorados? O trabalho explora o Aprendizado Profundo (Deep Learning) focado em Aprendizado Supervisionado
. A técnica central proposta é o Aumento por Recuperação (Retrieval Augmentation), que utiliza o método de Vizinhos Mais Próximos (Nearest Neighbors) para auxiliar na predição
. Foram utilizadas arquiteturas como LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) para decodificação e análise de séries temporais, CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks), especificamente o modelo ResNet pré-treinado no ImageNet, para codificação de imagens
. Além disso, foram explorados Mecanismos de Atenção (Attention Mechanisms), incluindo uma nova proposta de atenção multinível (multi-level attention)
. Para representações de texto, foram usados Sentence Transformers (RoBERTa) e embeddings estáticos (fastText)
. A busca de similaridade foi realizada através da biblioteca FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search)
.
QP5 - A arquitetura consta algum módulo de visualização computacional para explicabilidade de treino ou teste? Sim. O trabalho enfatiza que a abordagem aumenta a interpretabilidade do modelo
. Os autores fornecem uma visualização do mecanismo de atenção multinível, permitindo observar quanto peso o modelo atribui à imagem de entrada original versus a legenda recuperada do vizinho mais próximo durante a geração de texto
. Essa visualização é apresentada através de gráficos de barras que acompanham a geração de palavras (Figuras 2 e 4)
.
QP6 - Os dados utilizados para treino/teste/validação são explicados em sua completude e faz sentido para o problema alvo? Sim. Os autores utilizam dois datasets amplamente reconhecidos na literatura: o Flickr8k para legendagem de imagens (image captioning) e o IMDB para análise de sentimento
. O Flickr8k contém 8.000 imagens, cada uma com 5 legendas, e o IMDB possui 50.000 avaliações de filmes rotuladas como positivas ou negativas
. As divisões entre treino, validação e teste são detalhadas (ex: divisões de Karpathy para o Flickr8k), e os dados são apropriados para validar as tarefas de geração (captioning) e classificação (sentimento) propostas
.
QP7 - Os critérios de avaliação da arquitetura permitem avaliar várias tarefas multimodalidade? Sim. Para a tarefa multimodal de legendagem de imagens, foram aplicadas métricas de qualidade de texto consagradas: BLEU (1 a 4), METEOR, ROUGE L, CIDEr, SPICE e a métrica mais recente BERTScore
. Para a tarefa de análise de sentimento (monomodal), utilizaram-se Acurácia e F-score
. O conjunto de métricas permite uma avaliação abrangente tanto da precisão gramatical e semântica na multimodalidade quanto da eficácia na classificação
.

P488.title: On the Use of Graph Neural Networks for Virtual Network Embedding
P488.abstract: Resource allocation of 5G network slices is one of the most important challenges for network operators. It can be formulated using the Virtual Network Embedding (VNE) problem, which was and remains an active field of studies, also known because of its NP-hardness. Owing to its complexity, several heuristics, meta-heuristics and Deep Learning-based solutions have been proposed. However, these solutions are inefficient either due to their slowness or to not taking into account the structure of data which results in an inefficient exploration of the solutions space. To overcome these issues, in this work we unveil the potential of Graph Convolutional Neural (GCN) networks and Deep Reinforcement Learning techniques in solving the VNE problem. The key point of our approach is modeling of the VNE problem as an episodic Markov Decision Process which is solved in a Reinforcement Learning fashion using a GCN-based neural architecture. The simulation results highlight the efficiency of our approach through an increased performance over time, while outperforming state-of-art solutions in terms of the services' acceptance ratio.
P488.venue: 2020 International Symposium on Networks, Computers and Communications (ISNCC)

P489.title: SAND: Enhancing Open-Set Neuron Descriptions through Spatial Awareness
P489.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2, QS4
P489.abstract: We propose Spatially-Aware open-set Network Dissection (SAND), a technique to identify and label the learned representation of the neurons of deep vision networks. Con-trary to earlier open-vocabulary neuron explanation meth-ods, we also leverage a neuron's spatial pattern of activation to guide our predictions towards more accurate and rel-evant concepts, while avoiding being misled by confounding visual information. We highlight important regions for a neuron through image masking, which has the advantage of being able to block out irrelevant concepts from an im-age, handling irregularly shaped activation regions, and re-vealing the visual concepts that a neuron learns in order to identify objects. We use CLIP to connect highly activating image regions with descriptive concepts, and measure the quality of our results through human evaluation. Further, since such manual evaluation can be highly time consuming, costly, and unscalable, we also propose an automated approach which uses image generation to get quantitative feedback on the generated concepts. Finally, as an application of our interpretability method, we demonstrate how it can be tuned to the medical domain. Our code is available at https://github.com/Trustworthy-ML-LabISAND
P489.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)

P490.title: CAFuser: Condition-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Robust Semantic Perception of Driving Scenes
P490.abstract: Leveraging multiple sensors is crucial for robust semantic perception in autonomous driving, as each sensor type has complementary strengths and weaknesses. However, existing sensor fusion methods often treat sensors uniformly across all conditions, leading to suboptimal performance. By contrast, we propose a novel, condition-aware multimodal fusion approach for robust semantic perception of driving scenes. Our method, CAFuser, uses an RGB camera input to classify environmental conditions and generate a Condition Token that guides the fusion of multiple sensor modalities. We further newly introduce modality-specific feature adapters to align diverse sensor inputs into a shared latent space, enabling efficient integration with a single and shared pre-trained backbone. By dynamically adapting sensor fusion based on the actual condition, our model significantly improves robustness and accuracy, especially in adverse-condition scenarios. CAFuser ranks first on the public MUSES benchmarks, achieving 59.7 PQ for multimodal panoptic and 78.2 mIoU for semantic segmentation, and also sets the new state of the art on DeLiVER.

P491.title: EmoGen: Emotional Image Content Generation with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
P491.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2
P491.abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in image generation task, where users can create visually astonishing images with high-quality. However, existing text-to-image diffusion models are proficient in generating concrete concepts (dogs) but encounter challenges with more abstract ones (emotions). Several efforts have been made to modify image emotions with color and style adjustments, facing limitations in effectively conveying emotions with fixed image contents. In this work, we introduce Emotional Image Content Generation (EICG), a new task to generate semantic-clear and emotion-faithful images given emotion categories. Specifically, we propose an emotion space and construct a mapping network to align it with the powerful Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) space, providing a concrete interpretation of abstract emotions. Attribute loss and emotion confidence are further proposed to ensure the semantic diversity and emotion fidelity of the generated images. Our method outperforms the state-of-the-art text-to-image approaches both quantitatively and qualitatively, where we derive three custom metrics, i.e., emotion accuracy, semantic clarity and semantic diversity. In addition to generation, our method can help emotion understanding and inspire emotional art design. Project page: https://vcc.tech/research/2024/EmoGen.
P491.venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)

P492.title: TrTr-CMR: Cross-Modal Reasoning Dual Transformer for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
P492.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QS1, QS2, QS3
P492.abstract: Remote sensing image captioning (RSIC) is an interesting but challenging cross-modal reasoning task for computer vision and natural language processing. Most of the recent popular approaches for RSIC utilize encoder-decoder architectures, which focus on visual features captured by convolutional neural network (CNN)-based encoder and semantic information by recurrent neural network (RNN)-based or long short-term memory (LSTM)-based decoder, but encounter difficulties with multiscale, multicategories, and direction ambiguity challenges. To make the most of semantic understanding ability of Transformers, in this article, we propose a new attention-based visual-linguistic reasoning framework with dual Transformer for RSIC. Specifically, Swin Transformer (SwinT) encoder with shifted window partitioning scheme is introduced for multiscale visual feature extraction to discover the intrinsic relationship in the objects, and then, a Transformer language model (TLM) with self-attention and cross attention is designed as the decoder to generate a well-formed sentence for the image. Extensive experiments are conducted on the public RSIC benchmark datasets, including UCM-Captions, Sydney-Captions, and RSICD. The impressive performance verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. In addition, the source code and models of this work are publicly available at https://github.com/LianYi233/TrTr-CMR.
P492.venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

P493.title: Weakly Supervised Zero-Shot Medical Image Segmentation Using Pretrained Medical Language Models
P493.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QS2, QS3, QS4
P493.abstract: Deep learning segmentation models have traditionally suffered from the tyranny of annotation. In this paper, we propose a text-supervised, zero-shot approach to medical image segmentation. Briefly, we first pretrain a language encoder using contrastive learning. Then we use one positive prompt and one negative prompt. Our model learns to extract visual features aligned to the positive prompt and also learns to generate masks that can filter images such that they are aligned to the negative prompt. Eschewing human-annotated labels, our model is trained using only medical images associated with radiological reports. It achieves better zero-shot performance than other weakly/semi-supervised full-shot models on the segmentation of Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, Edema, Pleural Effusion, and Pneumothorax, and comparable performance on the segmentation of Lung Consolidation.
P493.venue: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)

P494.title: I-AI: A Controllable & Interpretable AI System for Decoding Radiologists’ Intense Focus for Accurate CXR Diagnoses
P494.codes: QP1, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2, QS3, QS4
P494.abstract: In the field of chest X-ray (CXR) diagnosis, existing works often focus solely on determining where a radiologist looks, typically through tasks such as detection, segmentation, or classification. However, these approaches are often designed as black-box models, lacking interpretability. In this paper, we introduce Interpretable Artificial Intelligence (I-AI) a novel and unified controllable interpretable pipeline for decoding the intense focus of radiologists in CXR diagnosis. Our I-AI addresses three key questions: where a radiologist looks, how long they focus on specific areas, and what findings they diagnose. By capturing the intensity of the radiologist’s gaze, we provide a unified solution that offers insights into the cognitive process underlying radiological interpretation. Unlike current methods that rely on black-box machine learning models, which can be prone to extracting erroneous information from the entire input image during the diagnosis process, we tackle this issue by effectively masking out irrelevant information. Our proposed I-AI leverages a vision-language model, allowing for precise control over the interpretation process while ensuring the exclusion of irrelevant features.To train our I-AI model, we utilize an eye gaze dataset to extract anatomical gaze information and generate ground truth heatmaps. Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate the efficacy of our method. We showcase that the attention heatmaps, designed to mimic radiologists’ focus, encode sufficient and relevant information, enabling accurate classification tasks using only a portion of CXR. The code, checkpoints, and data are at https://github.com/UARK-AICV/IAI.
P494.venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)

P495.title: Explain Me the Painting: Multi-Topic Knowledgeable Art Description Generation
P495.codes: QP1, QP3, QP5, QP6, QS1, QS2, QS3
P495.abstract: Have you ever looked at a painting and wondered what is the story behind it? This work presents a framework to bring art closer to people by generating comprehensive descriptions of fine-art paintings. Generating informative descriptions for artworks, however, is extremely challenging, as it requires to 1) describe multiple aspects of the image such as its style, content, or composition, and 2) provide background and contextual knowledge about the artist, their influences, or the historical period. To address these challenges, we introduce a multi-topic and knowledgeable art description framework, which modules the generated sentences according to three artistic topics and, additionally, enhances each description with external knowledge. The framework is validated through an exhaustive analysis, both quantitative and qualitative, as well as a comparative human evaluation, demonstrating outstanding results in terms of both topic diversity and information veracity.
P495.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

P496.title: A Proposal-Free One-Stage Framework for Referring Expression Comprehension and Generation via Dense Cross-Attention
P496.abstract: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) and Generation (REG) have become one of the most important tasks in visual reasoning, since it is an essential step for many vision-and-language tasks such as visual question answering or visual dialogue. However, it has not been widely used in many downstream tasks, mainly for the following reasons: 1) mainstream two-stage methods rely on additional annotations or off-the-shelf detectors to generate proposals. It would heavily degrade the generalization ability of models and lead to inevitable error accumulation. 2) Although one-stage strategies for REC have been proposed, these methods have to depend on lots of hyper-parameters (such as anchors) to generate bounding box. In this paper, we present a proposal-free one-stage (PFOS) framework that can directly regress the region-of-interest from the image or generate unambiguous descriptions in an end-to-end manner. Instead of using the dominant two-stage fashion, we take the dense-grid of images as input for a cross-attention transformer that learns multi-modal correspondences. The final bounding box or sentence is directly predicted from the image without the anchor selection or the computation of visual difference. Furthermore, we expand the traditional two-stage listener-speaker framework to jointly train by a one-stage learning paradigm. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on both accuracy and speed for comprehension and competitive results for generation.

P497.title: Knowledge-Driven Generative Adversarial Network for Text-to-Image Synthesis
P497.codes: QP1, QP3, QP5, QP6, QP7, QS1, QS2
P497.abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) synthesis is a challenging task that aims to convert natural language descriptions to real images. It remains an open problem mainly due to the diversity of text descriptions, which poses a huge obstacle in generating vivid and relevant images. Moreover, the existing evaluation metrics in T2I synthesis are mainly used to evaluate the visual quality of the generated images, while the semantic consistency between the two modalities is often ignored. To address these issues, we present a novel Knowledge-Driven Generative Adversarial Network, termed KD-GAN, and a new evaluation system, named Pseudo Turing Test (PTT for short). Concretely, KD-GAN takes a further step in imitating the behavior of human painting, i.e., drawing an image according to reference knowledge. The introduction of reference knowledge in KD-GAN not only improves the quality of the generated images but also enhances the semantic consistency between them and the input texts. In addition, KD-GAN can also greatly avoid some flaws against common sense during image generation, e.g., skiing in the blue sky. The proposed PTT is an important supplement to the existing evaluation system of T2I synthesis. It includes a set of pseudo-experts of different multimedia tasks to evaluate the semantic consistency between the given texts and the generated images. To validate the proposed KD-GAN, we conducted extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets, i.e., Caltech-UCSD Birds (CUB), and MS-COCO (COCO). The experimental results demonstrate that KD-GAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods on IS, FID, and the proposed PTT metrics.11The codes of KD-GAN are at [Online]. Available: https://github.com/pengjunn/KD-GAN and the codes and models of PTT are at [Online]. Available: https://github.com/pengjunn/PTT.
